Glint, 008 light-honest: street level against the paintings, on honest frames

2026-10-15. Inputs: Aster's brief, Latch's honest Editor path (commit 8235449, Capture), the eight 26 Sep paintings in briefs/008/concepts/. Changed: unity/Assets/Suborned/Editor/World/light.json only. Not changed: scenes, code, assets. The built scene still carries the old light until it is rebuilt (see Open issues).

Result

  • The orange was the grade, not the sun. The grade's highlights tint (1, 0.85, 0.66) is a full-strength multiplier (URP: weight 0 is not off); with the warm colour filter it pushed lit paving to R-B 63 to 69 on honest frames, where the paintings sit at 39 to 45. Both are neutral now; the sun keeps the warmth (colour unchanged, #ffe0d0).
  • Sun paving (237, 206, 174) to (237, 217, 198), the paintings' lit paving mean (240, 220, 201); dE2000 5.5 to 0.7 on the home frame, 1.7 to 2.3 on the other two. Over all measured sunlit surfaces the mean dE to the paintings falls 5.9 to 3.1 (all surfaces including shade, road and seafoam 7.4 to 4.7).
  • Shaded ivory stays ivory: shaded paving (183, 167, 150) to (170, 157, 146) (the paintings' shaded stone and paving mean (170, 160, 153), dE 2.1), R-B 24 (paintings 17 to 23). Shade over sun on paving, linear Y: 0.62 to 0.49 (the paintings 0.40 to 0.63; the play-angle painting 0.48). B5's 0.64 was measured on clipped frames; I traded some of it for painting-like depth, and it is one number (ambient x0.9) if Sky wants shade lighter.
  • Signals: every key surface now sits at least dE 22.5 from every signal colour (was 16.7: lit paving and stone were inside the guard amber's 20). Pixels within dE 20 of guard amber: home frame 51.5% to 2.8% (what is left is the yellow and peach roof accents and the ochre brick, the same pixels as before). Signals still draw unlit; the outside-the-grade pass is not built (open issues).
  • Form on lit paving is better, not worse: tile contrast on the home sun paving, luma std 3.6 to 6.9; no pixel at R 255 (R 246 or more: 9.1% to 4.5%).

Redline L7 (crossing light receives no shadows)

Not yet in the built scene; it lands at the next scene build, and it changes nothing you can see. CrossingKit.Lens sets _ReceiveShadows 0 and _RECEIVE_SHADOWS_OFF on the seafoam light (code as committed in 8235449). The saved material Assets/Scenes/HarbourDistrict-crosslight.mat (shader DecoKit/Lit Cutaway, 2,428 renderers use it) still has _ReceiveShadows 1 and no keyword, because it was written before the fix. The shader declares the keyword in its ForwardLit pass (DK_LitCutaway.shader line 126) and takes URP's forward pass, so the switch is honoured. In-memory check, asset restored and not saved: the kerb frame (crossing lights standing in the tower's shadow) rendered with the material receiving and not receiving shadows is pixel-identical (0 of 2,073,600 pixels differ, max 0): cost only, no look change. Frames: frames/l7-receive.png, l7-norecv.png.

Method

  • Every frame goes through Capture (ARGBHalf, MSAA as the URP asset's, sRGB blit): tools/GlintHonest.cs via the Unity MCP run_script, GPU Resident Drawer off, TacticalShadows as the play camera has them, people hidden for measuring (the perf player strips them) and visible for the sheet.
  • Candidates are applied in memory to the open scene (sun, trilight ambient, fog, sky material, a fresh grade profile built exactly as Atmosphere.Post builds it) and restored in a finally block: editor_status ready, scene isDirty false afterwards, sun 1.35 and the grade asset back. Nothing was saved or rebuilt.
  • Proof the harness is honest: with no candidate, and with the old light.json applied, the home frame equals Latch's editor-new-home.png to 0.00 mean level (max single-pixel difference 147, p99 0); the aerial uses a temporary camera cloned from cameras/docks.
  • dE2000 as tools/world/rules/deltae.ts (the Python port gives 33.9986 and 21.2949 for cones/guard and brass/guard, the same as the TypeScript).
  • Limits: reflection probes and the default reflection cube were baked under the old light and are not re-baked here (chrome, globes and glass in these frames still mirror the old sun until the build). The paintings differ among themselves by 5 to 12 levels per channel on lit paving; the target is their mean, the per-painting range is in the table.

Open issues and handoffs

  1. Scene rebuild (Latch): sun, ambient, fog and the grade asset are serialized in the scene, so light.json takes effect at Suborned/World > Build Harbour District (the world build; it also re-bakes the probes and lands L7). Done-check: Suborned/Perf/Warmth Probe home frame, sun paving about (237, 217, 198) and shaded paving (170, 157, 146) on the kerb frame; a perf player build for the player-side number (the grade and sun are the same code path, the old frames agreed to 0.8 levels). I did not rebuild: the tree holds other agents' uncommitted plan changes, and a 371 MB scene rebuild would mix them into this comparison.
  2. Signals outside the grade (Glyph, Latch): not built; swatch shifts above. Until then the contract line holds only for the unlit palette gate.
  3. Roof albedo (Vela, look.json): lit roofs paler (dE 7) and shaded roofs grey where the paintings are cream.
  4. Yellow and peach roof accents (Vela): lit about 224, 197, 72 and 254, 187, 151, within dE 20 of the guard amber (not new; the unlit-palette gate passes).
  5. Sky and haze were not touched; the skyline row is there to show nothing moved at distance. The terrain beyond the district is still sand tan (palette), against the hero painting's white city and blue water.
  6. Any look image Sky saw from the old Editor paths (B5 shots) was the clipped one; this sheet replaces them.
